requiredFindings.finding: The README requires 'Project the four inherited description overrides by stable file path without rewriting historical rows', but the selected lock records them as positional JSON Pointers with NO path field, and for all four the parent's description at that index equals the recorded `before`, which confirms index resolution. Inserting the new row at index 187 shifts every later index by one, so two of the four selectors land on different files: /files/502/description targets `package.json` in v58 but `docs/report.md` at the same index in v59, and /files/569/description targets `schemas/sources/imported-v1.schema.json` in v58 but `schemas/sources/import-source-context-v1.schema.json` in v59. (/files/7 and /files/13 are before the insertion point and are stable.) Both intended targets survive intact with unchanged descriptions at index 503 and 570 respectively, so path projection is achievable — what is missing is the record of it. successor.json, the machine-readable artefact a selection consumes, asserts five properties and none about the overrides; inheritedRowsEqualByValue concerns row values, not selector positions. Depending on the selection machinery the outcome is either a silent retarget of two selected description overrides onto unrelated files, or a selection failure, and the artefacts do not say which.
requiredFindings.required: Make the re-projection explicit in successor.json rather than in README prose. Either record a path alongside each selector so the override is keyed by path and the index becomes advisory, or declare the re-projected pointers for this candidate — /files/7 -> /files/7, /files/13 -> /files/13, /files/502 -> /files/503, /files/569 -> /files/570 — with the existing `before` text as verification that each landed on its intended row.
requiredFindings.note: no select script was run and no view is expressed on how root's selection tooling currently resolves these pointers; the point is that the artefacts do not say
